reason: The wet methane needs its own cold storage, so sending it to the methane liquefier seems like a useful first step.
expectation: I expect the plant to dry and liquefy the methane for storage, though it may need another step.

alternatives.reason: The oxygen also needs separate cold storage, and its liquefier looks appropriate; I chose to handle the wet methane first.

effect: The methane is dried and stored as a liquid, though filling the store will take months. The oxygen store remains to be prepared.
reaction: I was interested that the plant removes water before liquefaction and that filling the store takes so long.
reason: The oxygen needs its own cold store, and its liquefier is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the oxygen to be liquefied and stored separately, though it may need further preparation.

effect: The oxygen is now stored separately, completing both cold-storage goals and establishing the beginnings of a way off Mars.
reaction: The link between the two stores and the return journey made the result feel consequential.

mostWorthwhile.text: Storing the methane was most worthwhile because the result explained why the wet gas needed drying and showed that filling the store would take months.

leastWorthwhile.text: The oxygen step was less engaging because it was the only remaining combination and gave less detail about the process.

surprise.text: I was surprised that collecting the rest of the liquid methane would take months of power and water.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary: each supply had a matching liquefier and a clear storage goal.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the long fuel-making season and eventual return unfold. This chapter made that prospect tangible, though its choices were straightforward.
